text:
objective: To conduct a decadal analysis and simulation of land use and land cover (LULC) changes in Taiwan from 1990 to 2020 and project future LULC for 2030 and 2050 under multiple scenarios, incorporating demographic trends such as negative population growth, using machine learning and Markov chain models.
country: Taiwan
land_use_classes: barren; uncultivated; shallow water; deep water; built-up; forest; cultivated
baseline_years: 1990; 2000; 2010; 2020
target_future_years: 2030; 2050
scenarios: 2-variables (elevation, distance to road); 3-variables (elevation, distance to road, distance to river); 5-variables (aspect, elevation, hillshade, distance to river, slope); 6-variables (aspect, elevation, hillshade, distance to river, distance to road, slope)
analysis_methods: Supervised classification using maximum likelihood classifier; Support Vector Machine (SVM) for LULC classification; Markov-chain method for LULC simulation; accuracy assessment via confusion matrix, kappa coefficient, overall accuracy, producer’s and user’s accuracy; root-mean-square-error (RMSE) for error assessment
simulation_method_advantages: The SVM-Markov chain hybrid approach leverages precise LULC classification by SVM and probabilistic future prediction by Markov chain, improving accuracy in complex urban landscapes; it is among the first applications at a national scale for Taiwan and allows multi-scenario testing with environmental predictors.
predictors: aspect; elevation; hillshade; distance to river; distance to road; slope
population_selected: Yes
data_sources: Landsat 5/7/8 Surface Reflectance Tier 1 satellite images (1990–2020); Shuttle Radar Topographic Mission (SRTM) Digital Elevation Model (30 m); OpenStreetMap; Google Earth; Google Earth Engine (for image collection and preprocessing); ground control points (GCPs) for validation
tools_software_used: Google Earth Engine; GIS software (implied); SVM and Markov-chain modeling (specific software not named)
validation_performed: Yes
validation_methods: Confusion matrix; overall accuracy; kappa coefficient; producer’s accuracy; user’s accuracy; RMSE
validation_data_sources: Ground control points (GCPs): 655 points for historical classification validation; 300 points for 2020 simulated LULC validation
key_findings: Built-up area increased by ~140% from 1990 to 2020 and is projected to increase up to 223% by 2050 under the 6-variable scenario; barren and deep water areas declined significantly (~49–54%); forest and cultivated areas slightly increased; despite negative population growth, impervious surface expansion continues; the 3-variable scenario provided the most balanced and valid simulation results.
implications: Continued urban expansion despite declining population suggests inefficient land use and potential environmental risks; findings support the need for infill development, conservation planning, and green space integration; results can inform national land-use policy and decarbonization strategies in mid-sized, rapidly urbanizing economies.
limitations: Reliance on static transition probabilities in Markov model assumes stationarity, ignoring non-linear dynamics; exclusion of socio-economic drivers beyond population trends; moderate-resolution satellite imagery may limit urban classification accuracy; cloud cover restricted pre-1990 data use.
future_directions: Incorporate dynamic socio-economic variables and policy scenarios; integrate higher-resolution imagery or object-based classification for urban areas; extend carbon emission modeling linked to LULC projections; apply the framework to other island or mountainous regions with similar demographic transitions.
scalability: The methodology is scalable to other mid-sized, rapidly urbanizing countries with complex topography and demographic shifts, especially those with available satellite and geospatial data.
novelty: First national-scale LULC simulation study for Taiwan covering 1990–2050; integrates SVM classification with Markov-chain simulation; explicitly incorporates negative population growth into LULC forecasting; tests multiple environmental predictor scenarios to assess model sensitivity.
